Its due is when it comes off, three days after the fix's date, since twenty runs after the fix take about two and a quarter at the net's pace of about nine a day. That leaves room for about seven runs more, so a red run past the count's first seven, which starts it again, moves the due, and its owner sends the new one before this one passes. Only the media call's drops by the shaper can be told already, from the video tin it alone fills; with no call on in test_a_call_loses_little, the page call goes best effort beside the app's downloads. The router's fq_codel counts every flow together, and the builder's own losses are counted only for every flow together and printed only on a failure, so the fix counts both calls' own datagrams at each step of their path, the shaper's included, and prints them on a pass too. test_unshaped, with the shaper stopped, failed too, so its premise that the router alone meets the bar is in question, and the fix says what it bars rather than keep a bar the builder's own losses can break.
